title: Annotatio VI §.II Classis I.1: Judas at institution — no partaking (Lk 22; Jn 13)
pass_a_gloss: Of the FIRST CLASS the first Argument is supplied by the History of the Holy Supper’s Institution, in which Christ is said to have reclined at the sacred table with his twelve disciples, one of them being impious and meditating nefarious betrayal of his Lord (Lk 22:14 coll. v. 3). That this first unworthy Guest of the Sacred Feast in no way ate Christ’s Body, or was made partaker of it in any mode, is clear from this: that when he had received from Christ the morsel — the dipped bit of the Paschal feast preceding the Supper — Satan is said to have entered into him (Jn 13:27), having no communion with Christ and his body (2 Cor 6).
pass_b_english: Class I, argument 1: at the Supper’s institution Christ reclines with the Twelve, one impious and plotting betrayal (Lk 22:14 with v.3).
That first unworthy guest did not eat Christ’s body in any mode: after the dipped Paschal morsel, Satan entered him (Jn 13:27) — no communion with Christ and his body (2 Cor 6).
source_text: CLASSIS PRIMÆ Argumentum primum suppeditat Institutionis S. Cœnæ Historia, quâ Christus cum duodecim discipulis suis, mensæ S. accubuisse fertur, unô eorum impio existente & Domini sui nefariam proditionem meditante Luc. 22. 14. coll. cum vers. 3. Hunc, primum S. Epuli indignum Convivam, Corpus Christi neutiquam manducasse, vel istius ullo modo participem factum esse, inde constat, quod acceptô à Christo obsonio, seu intincto, Paschalis convivii, Cœnam antecedentis, frustulo, Satanas in ipsum intrasse dicitur Joh. 13. 27. nullam cum Christo ejusque corpore communionem habens 2. Cor. 6.
